question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

 

The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
option_1: Fresh bread was baked by the baker every morning.
option_2: Fresh bread are baked by the baker every morning.
option_3: Fresh bread is baked by the baker every morning.
option_4: Fresh bread is being baked by the baker every morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fresh bread is baked by the baker every morning.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The object of the active sentence, "fresh bread," becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the simple present verb "bakes" converts to "is baked", agreeing with the singular subject.

◦ Complete sentence: Fresh bread is baked by the baker every morning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...was baked..." — the simple past is wrongly used instead of the simple present "is baked".

 

• Option 2: "...are baked..." — the plural verb "are" wrongly disagrees with the singular subject "fresh bread"; it must be "is baked".

 

• Option 4: "...is being baked..." — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple passive "is baked".

 

NOTE

 

• The dairy delivers fresh milk every morning. → fresh milk is delivered by the dairy every morning (simple present active → simple present passive).

question:

option_4: The firefighters extinguished the fire within minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The firefighters extinguished the fire within minutes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The agent of the passive sentence, "the firefighters," becomes the subject, and the passive verb "was extinguished" (simple past) converts to the active simple past "extinguished".

◦ Complete sentence: The firefighters extinguished the fire within minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...extinguish the fire..." — the simple present is wrongly used instead of the simple past "extinguished".

 

• Option 2: "...have extinguished the fire..." — the present perfect is wrongly used instead of the simple past "extinguished".

 

• Option 3: "...were extinguishing the fire..." — the past continuous is wrongly used instead of the simple past "extinguished".

 

NOTE

 

• The window was broken by the storm within seconds. → the storm broke the window within seconds (simple past passive → simple past active).

question:

• Option 4: "...is generally being respected." — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple passive "is respected".

question:

Additional Information

NOTE

 

• The trainer told the recruits to assemble early. → the recruits were told by the trainer to assemble early (verb + object + to-infinitive, retained in the passive).

question: Select the option that is expressed in passive voice.
option_1: The pilot is flying the aircraft smoothly.
option_2: The passengers boarded the flight on time.
option_3: The aircraft was inspected thoroughly by the engineers.
option_4: The crew will serve breakfast shortly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The aircraft was inspected thoroughly by the engineers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A sentence is in the passive voice when its subject receives the action rather than performing it, typically formed with "be + past participle". Only "The aircraft was inspected thoroughly by the engineers" fits this structure.

◦ The aircraft was inspected thoroughly by the engineers — is in the passive voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "The pilot is flying the aircraft..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "the pilot" performs the action.

 

• Option 2: "The passengers boarded the flight..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "the passengers" performs the action.

 

• Option 4: "The crew will serve breakfast..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "the crew" performs the action.

 

NOTE

 

• Identify the passive sentence among: "The chef cooked the soup." / "The soup was cooked by the chef." → "The soup was cooked by the chef." (subject receives the action, formed with "be" + past participle).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

 

Several errors have been corrected by the editor in the final draft.
option_1: The editor corrected several errors in the final draft.
option_2: The editor has corrected several errors in the final draft.
option_3: The editor is correcting several errors in the final draft.
option_4: The editor had corrected several errors in the final draft.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The editor has corrected several errors in the final draft.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The present perfect passive ("have been corrected") converts to the active present perfect: "has corrected".

◦ Complete sentence: The editor has corrected several errors in the final draft.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...corrected several errors..." — the simple past is wrongly used instead of the present perfect "has corrected".

 

• Option 3: "...is correcting several errors..." — the present continuous is wrongly used instead of the present perfect "has corrected".

 

• Option 4: "...had corrected several errors..." — the past perfect is wrongly used instead of the present perfect "has corrected".

 

NOTE

 

• Several changes have been suggested by the reviewer in the manuscript. → the reviewer has suggested several changes in the manuscript (present perfect passive → present perfect active).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

 

The assistant must submit the minutes of the meeting by tomorrow.
option_1: The minutes of the meeting must submitted by the assistant by tomorrow.
option_2: The minutes of the meeting should be submitted by the assistant by tomorrow.
option_3: The minutes of the meeting must be submitted by the assistant by tomorrow.
option_4: The minutes of the meeting must be submitting by the assistant by tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The minutes of the meeting must be submitted by the assistant by tomorrow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the modal "must", the passive form is "must be + past participle": "must submit" becomes "must be submitted".

◦ Complete sentence: The minutes of the meeting must be submitted by the assistant by tomorrow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "must submitted" — the auxiliary "be" is missing; the correct form is "must be submitted".

 

• Option 2: "should be submitted" — the modal "should" wrongly replaces "must", changing the degree of obligation.

 

• Option 4: "must be submitting" — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple modal passive "must be submitted".

 

NOTE

 

• The clerk must file the report by evening. → the report must be filed by the clerk by evening (modal "must" + base verb → "must be" + past participle).
